description:
Implement the spec in .openspec/specs/deterministic-preflight/spec.md: add a deterministic preflight to the factory's checks gate stage so the line proves life mechanically before any model station runs. Pipeline for this order is sdlc-default (software domain, full reviewer set), selected by the run workflow. The run touches the gate and runner code that computes the run delta and executes the suite, the run report writer, the configuration surface for the declared smoke command and the declared public API list, and tests. Standard library only.

SEQUENCING GATE: this order is filed and staged only. Execute it only after the capability program resumption has completed (items 8 to 10 merged into anvil/capability-adds, the program merged to main, and the model migration landed), because preflight builds on the merged checks gate and shares its code with the program's remaining items. Do not execute while the gateway billing balance is exhausted. If the program is not in main when the run starts, stop and report instead of running.

Build, per the spec requirements:

R1, import integrity: for each new or changed test file in the run delta, parse it with Python ast and collect its imports (package relative imports resolved against the file's package). The file must import at least one module from the delta's implementation set (the new or changed non-test modules). A test file importing none of them fails preflight by name. Unchanged pre-existing test files are not judged.

R2, execution proof: run the project suite under execution tracing (stdlib trace or an equivalent stdlib mechanism) inside the gate stage. Every changed implementation module must show executed lines; every changed or new function or method in them must show at least one execution, or it is named. A green suite that executed none of the changed code fails preflight. Record per module and per function counts in the run evidence.

R3, wiring: every public function or class introduced by the delta must be referenced from non-test code or a declared entry point. The work order format gains a declared public API list; names on it are exempt by name and the exemption is recorded as a run input. Additions referenced only from tests, or from nowhere, are named findings. This order's own work order declares no public API exemptions for itself.

R4, liveness smoke: when the project configuration declares a smoke command, run it in preflight after the suite; a non-zero exit is a preflight failure recorded as a smoke failure. When none is declared, record the step as not declared and do not fail.

R5, placement and reporting: preflight runs inside the existing checks gate stage, before any model station, consuming the gate's recorded base ref and delta; the gate's protected path rules and S4 base ref config resolution do not change behavior. A preflight failure returns the named findings to the builder as a pre-review gate loopback and launches zero reviewers. The run report records the preflight outcome and findings in a field set of its own, distinct from the checks result and from review verdicts.

R6, regression fixtures: the order's tests encode two fixtures modelled on the factory's own record and one healthy control: (a) the facade fixture, a delta whose test files pass while importing none of the implementation set (issue 9's 23 facade tests); (b) the unwired fixture, a delta whose new public function is implemented and unit tested but never referenced from non-test code (issue 21); (c) a healthy control whose tests import, execute and wire the changed code. Preflight must convict (a) under R1 and (b) under R3 with the right names, and pass (c). The fixtures are minimal trees constructed by the tests, not copies of historical projects.

Self application: this order's own execution runs the new preflight against its own delta on the factory repo, and the run evidence records that outcome. The factory suite must stay green; the new tests are part of the suite.

Guardrails: Python standard library only, no new dependency. Frozen surfaces: the review parse contract and parse_review semantics, the canonical review contract wording, the reviewer prompts and their Output Format sections, the review producer mechanisms (scoped reviewer writes, no stdout transcription), and the checks gate's S4 base ref behavior. No em dash or en dash character in any produced file (project style rule). The reviewer writes its review to the authoritative review file named in its packet; prose outside that file is not a review. Nothing in this order publishes anything.

GitHub issue: https://github.com/arananet/anvil-factory/issues/28
title: Deterministic preflight: proof of life before model spend
